messages:
rachel: FYI OSS feed flagged a vuln in orjson < 3.9.1 — potential deserialization RCE (CVE-2026-ORJSON). link: https://nvd.example/CVE-2026-ORJSON
alex: thanks. EPSS? CVSS? any PoC seen in the wild?
maria: EPSS 0.62, NVD CVSS 7.8 (temporal not set). I couldn't find a public PoC yet, but GitHub issues show exploit attempts in a couple of repos.
jon: which services pull orjson in prod? quick scan: events-ingest, metrics-processor, audit-serializer, preview-worker.
rachel: events-ingest is reachable via customer payloads (ingest-api). metrics-processor is internal only. audit-serializer runs in Dedicated and signs logs before upload.
alex: immediate ask: can we patch by bumping to 3.9.1? any breaking changes?
maria: quick test in staging: bump to 3.9.1, run existing deserialization tests — preview-worker fails due to new strict type check in one helper. small code tweak (wrap in try/except) fixes.
jon: rollout plan suggestion: 1) patch preview-worker + test 2) patch events-ingest behind canary 3) patch other internal services.
security-bot: created issue SEC-3421, severity: high, owner: @alex, SLA: 72h, links: https://tracker/SEC-3421
alex: assigning myself. I'll do preview-worker fix first. Can @maria run a quick dependency tree to ensure no nested libs reintroduce vulnerable orjson?
maria: running `pipdeptree -w silence | grep -i orjson -n` on services now — posting results in thread.
(rachel uploads): ```
# events-ingest requirements.txt
orjson==3.8.5
# preview-worker requirements.txt
orjson==3.8.5
# metrics-processor requirements.txt
orjson==3.9.0
```
jon: note: metrics-processor already at 3.9.0 (ok). events-ingest + preview-worker need bumps.
alex: important: audit-serializer is used to sign logs; ensure patch doesn't change serialization format (checksum). @rachel can you run a quick integration compare for signed payloads?
rachel: will do. quick note: if we need to rotate signatures, KMS interaction might be required; but patch should be backwards-compatible — I'll validate.
maria: triage suggestion: CVSS 7.8 (High) based on AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H, EPSS moderately high => prioritize events-ingest canary within 24h, full rollout 48-72h.
alex: agreed. I'll open PR for preview-worker now, tag for canary deploy. anyone object to emergency patch pipeline? :thumbsup:
jon: :thumbsup: go for it. also add a vuln note to the repo README (patch tracking).
security-bot: updated SEC-3421 with status: triage complete; action: patch-in-progress; ETA: 36h
rachel: after patch we should add a short e2e: send a crafted payload (sanity) to events-ingest to verify no unexpected behavior.
alex: noted. will request canary traffic and add observability hooks (slow logs, exceptions metric).
maria: will follow up with dependency PRs for other services and a roll-forward plan.
jon: if PoC appears, escalate to incident channel and consider temporary WAF rule to block suspicious payloads.
rachel: marking thread: watch-for-exploit, and adding cross-team owners: @alex (owner), @maria (deps), @jon (mitigation).
